html:
Formatting an ebook used to mean either paying for expensive software like Vellum or spending days learning Sigil and Calibre. Neither option was great for authors who just want to get their book published without a technical detour.

In 2026, you can format a professional-quality ebook for free — and do it in a fraction of the time. Here's exactly how.

What "Formatting" Actually Means

Ebook formatting isn't about making your book look pretty on screen — that's design. Formatting is the structural process of turning your manuscript into a file that reading platforms can parse, display, and distribute correctly.

A properly formatted ebook has:

  • Valid EPUB structure (mimetype, container, OPF manifest, spine)
  • Clean HTML chapter files without Word formatting artifacts
  • A functional table of contents (NCX or nav document)
  • Properly declared metadata (title, author, language, identifier)
  • Images that are correctly referenced and sized
  • CSS that's compatible with e-readers

Miss any of these and you get platform rejections, broken formatting on devices, or a poor reader experience. The good news is that you can handle all of it without paying for software.

Step 1: Clean Your Manuscript First

The biggest source of EPUB errors isn't the EPUB itself — it's what you bring into it from Word or Google Docs. Before you do anything else, clean your manuscript.

Upload your .docx file to the Word Cleanup Checker. It scans for:

  • Double spaces (cause inconsistent spacing in ebooks)
  • Straight quotes (should be curly smart quotes)
  • Double hyphens (should be em dashes)
  • Stacked blank paragraphs (create irregular spacing)
  • Trailing spaces at line ends
  • Manually applied bold or italic formatting across entire paragraphs

The checker is read-only — it identifies problems without modifying your file. Review the report, make corrections in Word, then download the cleaned version before moving to conversion. This step alone prevents dozens of EPUB errors later.

Step 2: Convert to EPUB

Once your manuscript is clean, convert it to EPUB. The Full Manuscript Mode handles this in one step:

  1. Upload your cleaned .docx or .txt file
  2. It detects chapter headings automatically
  3. Generates clean EPUB 3.0 HTML for each chapter
  4. Builds the OPF manifest and navigation document
  5. Returns a valid EPUB 3.0 file ready to validate

This is free, runs in your browser, and takes about 30 seconds for a typical novel. The output is lean HTML without the ghost spacing and inline style bloat that conversion tools like Calibre typically produce.

Step 3: Build Your Metadata

Your ebook needs metadata for every platform you're publishing to. KDP, Apple Books, Kobo, IngramSpark, and Draft2Digital all want slightly different metadata formats.

Use the Metadata Builder to fill in your book's information once and get properly formatted metadata for every platform at once. It outputs:

  • EPUB OPF metadata you can paste directly into your package file
  • KDP-formatted metadata fields
  • IngramSpark metadata format
  • Draft2Digital format

This is also free with no account required. Getting metadata right matters for discoverability — a mismatched title or author name between your EPUB and your platform listing causes ingestion errors at several distributors.

Step 4: Validate Your EPUB

Before uploading anywhere, validate your EPUB. This is the step most authors skip and the reason most EPUB rejections happen.

Upload your EPUB to the EPUB Validator. It checks:

  • Mimetype and container structure
  • OPF manifest completeness
  • Table of contents (NCX and nav)
  • HTML validity for every chapter file
  • Image references and file existence
  • CSS compatibility
  • Accessibility compliance (for Apple Books requirements)

The report shows you pass/fail for each check with specific error messages. Fix what it flags, re-upload to the validator, confirm everything passes, then upload to your publishing platform.

Step 5: Check Your Cover

Your cover image needs to meet each platform's size and format requirements. KDP requires a minimum of 1000 x 1600px (2:3 ratio). Apple Books wants at least 1400px on the shortest side. File format must be JPEG or PNG.

Upload your cover to the Cover Checker before embedding it in your EPUB or uploading it separately. It checks pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, file size, and format against the requirements of every major platform in one pass.

Step 6: Upload and Distribute

Once your EPUB passes validation and your cover is verified, you're ready to upload.

For Amazon KDP, go to kdp.amazon.com and create a new ebook title. Upload your EPUB directly — KDP handles the Kindle format conversion automatically. Upload your cover separately through KDP's interface, not embedded in the EPUB.

For Apple Books, use Apple Books Connect (authors.apple.com). Upload your validated EPUB. Apple's validation is stricter than KDP's, which is why the validator step matters more for Apple.

For wide distribution (Kobo, B&N, Google Play, library platforms), consider using Draft2Digital or PublishDrive as aggregators. Upload your EPUB once, they distribute to multiple platforms simultaneously.

Total Cost of This Workflow

The complete workflow described above uses:

  • Word Cleanup Checker — free
  • Full Manuscript Mode — free
  • Metadata Builder — free
  • EPUB Validator — free
  • Cover Checker — free

Zero cost. No subscription. No software to install. For most authors publishing standard prose books, this workflow produces a publish-ready EPUB that passes validation on every major platform.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need Calibre or Sigil to format an ebook?

Not anymore. Calibre and Sigil are powerful free tools but require significant time to learn. For most prose books, a browser-based workflow that handles conversion, validation, and metadata is faster and less error-prone.

How long does it take to format a novel for ebook using this workflow?

For a novel with standard chapter structure, the full process from clean manuscript to validated EPUB takes about 30–60 minutes — mostly spent reviewing the validation report and making any corrections.

Can I format a children's picture book or heavily illustrated book this way?

Illustrated books require more careful handling than text-based books. Image placement, sizing, and the relationship between text and images needs more attention. The free tools handle the structural EPUB requirements, but layout-intensive books may need additional manual work in the EPUB file itself.

What if my book has a complex table of contents with parts, sections, and chapters?

Hierarchical TOCs (with nested entries for parts and chapters) are supported in EPUB 3.0. If your manuscript uses consistent heading levels (H1 for parts, H2 for chapters), a good converter will build the hierarchy automatically.

Do I need an ISBN to format an ebook?

An ISBN isn't required to publish on KDP or many other platforms — you can use a platform-assigned identifier. But an ISBN is required for distribution through IngramSpark and is recommended if you want your book to appear in library catalogs and offline book databases. The Metadata Builder lets you enter either your own ISBN or a placeholder identifier.
